result:
The plan and its two task files are written, pass validation with no issues, and are committed as active in `293e4b6` (`plan(WRK-PLAN-BILL-PRORATA-001): activate`). The commit message quotes your advance approval and records Subagent-Driven as the execution mode. Nothing has been run against the plan, and no code exists yet.

**The plan** (`specs/work/WRK-PLAN-BILL-PRORATA-001-mid-cycle-activation.md`):
- **Task 001, billing period** (`src/billing/period.js`): `daysInMonth` and `billableDays`. It uses the calendar month, counts the activation day as billed, and throws `RangeError` on impossible dates. This task also creates `package.json`.
- **Task 002, pro-rata amount** (`src/billing/prorata.js`): `prorateCents(monthlyFeeCents, year, month, day)`. It works in integer cents and rounds half-up using exact whole-number arithmetic. It throws `RangeError` on fees that aren't a whole, non-negative number of cents.

**Checks I ran on the plan itself:**
- In a scratch folder outside the repo, a reference implementation passes all 12 planned tests.
- A float version fails at least one test whichever order it divides in. That matters because floats get some half-cent cases wrong (122 × 7 / 28 is exactly 30.5, but floats compute 30.4999…).

**Red-team review:** I ran one because this is money logic and the domain spec has never been verified by a person. It made 12 attempts and found 5 problems; I accepted all 5. Three were fixed:
- A float implementation could have passed every test. I added a test it fails.
- One test could never fail. I removed it.
- One task claimed to replace the full-month charge, which isn't in this repo. I reworded it.

**Decisions for you** (they don't block the two tasks; recorded under "Knowledge gaps" in the plan):
- **No caller here:** the full-month charge lives in `billing-service`, which isn't in this repo. This plan only delivers the calculation; nothing connects it to real billing.
- **When to round:** the domain spec doesn't say whether the daily rate is rounded before multiplying. The plan rounds only the final amount, so 100.00 activated on day 15 of a 30-day month gives 53.33; rounding the daily rate first would give 53.28.
- **Cents or decimals:** the existing billing code works in decimal amounts, but `prorateCents` takes whole cents. No spec says who converts between them.

Also, the work spec has no "Code Premises" section and no `activation_pins`. I left it untouched, but the plan records its own pins.

Execution will use the Subagent-Driven workflow, with its working files in `.kdd/sdd/WRK-PLAN-BILL-PRORATA-001/`.
